newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals mixed early, gold down, PGMs up.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals mixed early, gold down, PGMs up.

text.p: COMEX gold and silver futures were lower early Friday, but NYMEX platinum group metal (PGM) futures were higher, with no sign yet of a return of Russian platinum group metal (PGM) supplies to the market.

"We saw a little fresh selling in gold and silver on the open, but volumes are very light, and it will be interesting to see the open interest data for Thursday later this morning, after a big jump in open interest Wednesday," North American Equity Services COMEX floor trader John Geraghty said.
COMEX August gold was down $1.90 at $340.50 an ounce early, after bouncing Thursday following a slide to a new contract low at $340.20.

COMEX gold open interest jumped 10,437 lots to 174,844 contracts Wednesday, as funds were seen adding to short positions to take advantage of the weak downtrend of the past few months, but some short covering was noted Thursday, traders said.
But with the OTC options expiry in London due next week, traders did not expect gold prices to stray too far from the $340 strike price.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $338.90/40 an ounce early, compared to the London Friday morning fix at $339.55, and the New York close Thursday around $340.20/70.

On Wednesday spot gold closed around $338.90/40 in New York, not far from the four year low around $336.50 seen in February, but spot gold has found support around $340 an ounce four times since the year-to-date lows were seen.
COMEX July silver was down 2.5 cents at $4.720 an ounce, but July silver has been in a $4.65-4.90 range since mid-May.
NYMEX July platinum was up $2.30 at $415.00 an ounce, while NYMEX September palladium was up $2.60 at $172.80.
"After this week's slide in platinum and palladium, there's nothing much left on the downside, so you've got to like it down here," one NYMEX floor trader said.

In the physical market, the acute shortage of metal was pushing short term lease rates even higher, with one month palladium lease rates seen around 130 percent early Friday and one month platinum around 80 pct.

But market talk about a large platinum OTC call option at the $400 strike price, written by a Swiss bank and held by a U.S. bank, which expires next week was likely to keep the pressure on platinum prices, traders said.
Russian platinum group metal (PGM) exports, suspended for five months, are due to resume in late June, with Friday June 20 often mentioned by Russian officials as a likely re-start date.

But the first metal received by the U.S. arm of Almaz, the Russian metal export agency, would likely be shipped out to Zurich and Japanese customers, where Almaz is believed to have more pressing commitments, traders said.
Russia supplies about 60 pct of the world's palladium and 25 pct of its platinum.
